title: Square Root Functions
intro: f(x)=√(x−h)+k starts at the point (h,k) and grows slowly to the right. Domain: inside ≥ 0. Inverse of a piece of a parabola.

cards.title: Graphs of Square Root Functions
body: **Graphs of Square Root Functions.** The principal square root √x is defined for x ≥ 0 and is never negative.
Domain of y = √(g(x)) is where g(x) ≥ 0. Shifts: √(x − h) + k moves the graph right h and up k.
To solve √A = B, square both sides only when B ≥ 0, then check for extraneous roots.

cards.title: Square root functions
body: The basic square root function is f(x) = √x. Its graph starts at (0, 0) and rises more and more slowly to the right. The general form f(x) = a√(x − h) + k moves the starting point
**Domain:** the expression under the root must be ≥ 0, so for √(x − h) the domain is x ≥ h. **Range** (with a > 0): y ≥ k.

cards.title: Solving Square Root Equations
body: **Solving Square Root Equations.** The principal square root √x is defined for x ≥ 0 and is never negative.
Domain of y = √(g(x)) is where g(x) ≥ 0. Shifts: √(x − h) + k moves the graph right h and up k.
To solve √A = B, square both sides only when B ≥ 0, then check for extraneous roots.

tips.text: After squaring both sides of an equation with √, always substitute back — squaring can invent false roots.
